observations: Three photos show blue plastic drums with red snap-on lids, photographed outdoors on a sandy/wet lot.
Each drum has a hand-written number in marker on the lid or body ('15', '54') - looks like a seller's lot/stock number, not a capacity or brand marking.
A small rectangular sticker is visible on the side of the drum in photos 0 and 2, but the text on it is too small/blurry to read.
Watermark across the photos reads 'AJAOS BUILDING MATERIALS' - this is the seller's business stamp, not a product brand.
Other drums and buckets of different colours are visible in the background, indicating a yard selling multiple used containers.
No ruler, tape measure, or water-fill reference is present in any photo to confirm volume.
Surfaces look used - some scuffing and dirt, but no visible cracks or holes from this angle.

identity.kind: 120 liter plastic storage drum with lid

claims.evidence: No scale, ruler, or capacity marking is readable in photo 0, 1, or 2; size can only be guessed from proportion to the person's foot in photo 1.

risks.risk: Actual capacity may be smaller or larger than stated 120L.
risks.proof: A photo of the embossed capacity mark on the drum body, or the drum next to a tape measure/known-size object.
risks.if_unproven: priced as the smallest plausible drum size consistent with the photos (worst case)

risks.risk: Drum may have previously held chemicals or non-food-grade substances, affecting safe reuse.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the sticker/label on the side showing prior contents or a food-grade recycling symbol.

risks.risk: Hidden cracks, warping, or a damaged lid seal not visible from the current angles.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the base, the lid gasket, and a shot of the drum filled with water to confirm no leaks.
risks.if_unproven: priced as leak risk (lower tier) until shown intact

risks.risk: Drum could be heavily sun-faded or brittle from prolonged outdoor storage, shortening its usable life.
risks.proof: A photo showing the drum wall thickness or a flex/press test video.

proof_requests: Close-up of any embossed liter capacity marking on the drum body.
Clear photo of the side sticker/label text.
Photo or short video of the drum filled with water to confirm no leaks and true volume.
Close-up of the lid seal and base for cracks or repairs.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable by type as a used blue plastic drum with lid; its exact liter capacity, prior contents, and structural soundness are unverified from the photos, so it must be priced at the worst-case assumptions until the seller supplies the listed proofs.
